deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 154, 1983-84). Grothendieck studies systems Σ of n pseudo-lines in the real projective plane X. On the preceding pages he builds a compact cellular surface by gluing polygonal discs along 'arcs of specialisation'. The surface parametrises the combinatorial positions of an extra pseudo-line L relative to Σ. On the previous page he has already filled the 'quasi-regular holes' (circuits of incidence lines). What remains is to handle exceptional (= semi-critical) positions and specialisations, where L comes to coincide with a line D_i of Σ.

This page:
(1) The polygon Δ_L. Take L = D_i and treat it as the line at infinity of the reduced system (X, Σ∖{D_i}). The affine complement X∖D_i is an open disc whose boundary doubly covers D_i. The remaining n−1 pseudo-lines become a system of order n−1 inscribed in that disc (in modern terms an affine arrangement or wiring diagram). Their 2(n−1) ends on the boundary are the meeting points with D_i. They make the boundary a combinatorial polygon of order 2(n−1), which models the topological polygon Δ_L.
(2) The specialisation L → D. Consider a specialisation arc of L in a corridor ('couloir') of Σ∪{L} bounded by L and D_∞. On Δ_L the operation 'pulls' the arc across the corridors lying between it and D_∞, over D. This eliminates the region between L and D. The figure shows a disc with a green boundary (D_∞), a dotted vertical line D, orange pseudo-lines, a shaded half-disc being swept, and labels x, x', y, y'. The pull continues until the pairs y, y' become adjacent.
(3) The canonical identification. The resulting configuration is canonically isomorphic to (D, Δ_D), the disc with D taken as line at infinity. The new boundary arc (blue dotted) is canonically isomorphic, as a combinatorial pseudo-segment, to the old one. Grothendieck proposes to proceed 'as before' and identify Δ_L ≅ Δ_D by this isomorphism. This yields a transition isomorphism ω(Δ_L) → ω(Δ_D), i.e. ω(L) → ω(D), where ω is probably the orientation/boundary-orientation datum. He compares it with the tautological isomorphism (the exact relation is hard to read).
(4) The obstruction. Read backwards on Δ_D, these specialisations become 'W' arcs of generalisation, two for each vertex of D. The trouble is that arcs belonging to different vertices of D overlap ('empiètent les uns sur les autres'), so the naive gluing does not give a surface.
(5) The fix (next page). Replace each D by its 'contact elements' (D, s), one copy per vertex s on D. For a simple vertex the two exceptional generalisation arcs bound a topological bigon. For a multiple vertex they bound, together with the two ordinary generalisation arcs, a convex topological polygon. Gluing these bigons and polygons completes a compact surface.

In modern terms: Grothendieck is constructing, by explicit cell gluing, the space of all pseudo-lines that can be added to a fixed arrangement, i.e. the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid, or the 'dual topological plane'. A degenerate position L = D is a point that must be resolved by a combinatorial real blow-up: the link of the dual point D*, with one sector pair per vertex of D.
errors: No mathematical error, but the page records a failed attempt: identifying Δ_L ≅ Δ_D and gluing along generalisation arcs fails when D carries several vertices, because the arcs overlap. Grothendieck flags this himself ('L'ennui ici...'), and the remedy (multiplying D into contact elements (D,s)) comes on the next page.
The comparison of the transition isomorphism ω(Δ_L)→ω(Δ_D) with the tautological isomorphism is stated without verification; the nature of ω is not defined on this page.
The stopping condition for the 'pulling' ('until y, y' become adjacent; x, x' ...') is only sketched; well-definedness of the canonical isomorphism with non-simple vertices is not checked.

ideas.what: Taking one pseudo-line as line at infinity turns the projective system into a system of order n−1 inscribed in a disc, with a combinatorial boundary polygon of order 2(n−1)
ideas.modern_name: affine/wiring-diagram representation of a pseudoline arrangement; localisation (contraction) of a rank-3 oriented matroid at an element
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman (1980, wiring diagrams); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences); Folkman–Lawrence

ideas.what: Moves of a new pseudo-line across vertices (specialisation/generalisation arcs) glued into a compact cellular surface parametrising all positions of an added pseudo-line
ideas.modern_name: extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid; dual pseudoline arrangement / topological projective plane containing the arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu, 'Arrangements and topological planes' (1994)

ideas.what: Degenerate positions (L coinciding with D) resolved by replacing D with its contact elements (D,s), giving bigons or convex polygons
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial real (oriented) blow-up of the dual point D*; link of a multiple point in the dual arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in real blow-up / arrangement theory; no specific attribution

ideas.what: Transition isomorphisms ω(Δ_L)→ω(Δ_D) attached to specialisation, compared with the tautological one (gluing data / cocycle viewpoint)
ideas.modern_name: gluing (descent) data for a cellular surface; monodromy of orientation data

missed.claim: By 1983-84 Grothendieck was explicitly building the space of extensions of a pseudoline arrangement as a compact cellular surface. He resolved the exceptional points L = D by a contact-element blow-up. This anticipates the rank-3 extension-space results of Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) and the dual-plane construction of Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu (1994), and is not credited to him.
missed.quote: Il est donc tentant de procéder comme tantôt, et de vérifier Δ_L ≃ Δ_D par cet iso. canonique ... L'ennui ici, c'est que ces arcs de généralisation empiètent les uns sur les autres !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point. His explicit cell model, with (D,s) blow-ups and bigons for simple vertices, could also give a hands-on description of the rank-3 extension space as a sphere or projective plane. That matters since the general extension space conjecture is now known to fail (G. Liu).

missed.claim: The pages tie pseudoline combinatorics to his 'cartographic' viewpoint: surfaces given by graphs Γ=(S, Ā, σ, τ) with free edges, glued from polygonal discs, as in the Esquisse/dessins framework of the same years.
missed.quote: un polygone combinatoire, qui ... les polygones topologiques Δ_L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a potential bridge between oriented matroid extension spaces and combinatorial maps/dessins. It is not developed in the literature, though possibly only notational.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working step in an unpublished, early cellular construction of the extension space of a pseudoline arrangement (dual topological plane), predating Sturmfels–Ziegler and Goodman–Pollack et al. It is historically notable, but this particular page mostly records an obstacle whose resolution is standard in spirit (blow-up by contact elements).
transcription_corrections: First lines: likely 'on trouve un syst. de [pseudo-droites inscrit dans un disque], et les lieux de rencontre [avec le bord de] ce disque, correspondant aux éléments de Σ∖{D_i}'.
'à un soulier de Σ∪{L}, de covers (L, D∞)' should almost certainly read 'à un couloir de Σ∪{L}, de bords (L, D_∞)'.
'est L → D' is probably '[spécialisation] L → D'.
'de vérifier Δ_L ≃ Δ_D' is probably 'd'identifier Δ_L ≃ Δ_D'.
'Chaque moment de D détermine donc arcs de généralisation' is probably 'Chaque sommet de D détermine donc [deux] arcs de généralisation' (consistent with the next page).
Previous page 'en considérant D_i comme pr. pr.' is plausibly 'comme dr. à l'inf.' (line at infinity), matching the D_∞ notation and the disc picture.
'de ordre (n−1)' refers to the system of pseudo-lines of order n−1 inscribed in the polygon; the marginal insertion is 'd'ordre 2(n−1)' for the polygon.
